findings.title: Embedded-post author color inverts the lightness conversion
findings.body: The embedded-post author link was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). This change replaces it with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original lightness on $primary for light themes and uses the complement (100 minus that value) on $secondary for dark themes, which here would be 30% / 70%. The arguments are swapped, so light themes get a much lighter gray (weaker contrast on the light background) and dark themes get the value that was meant for light themes.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length color is inverted versus desktop
findings.body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The mobile rule is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The desktop counterpart in this same PR correctly keeps 70% on $primary and uses 30% on $secondary. Light-theme mobile hint text therefore becomes substantially darker than before and no longer matches desktop, and the dark-theme value is the old light-theme color rather than the complement.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness collapsed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: .topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). It is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), which matches the h4 directly below rather than the original 20%. The desktop .topic-map h3 in this PR correctly becomes 20% on $primary and 80% on $secondary. Light-theme mobile map headings get lighter, lower-contrast text, and dark themes do not get the complementary secondary scale.

findings.title: Group member name color no longer uses the original 30% lightness
findings.body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), intentionally darker than the sibling .title at 50%. It is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), identical to .title. Light themes lose that distinction and render names lighter than before; dark themes get a 50% secondary scale instead of the 70% complement used for every other 30% conversion in this PR.

findings.title: Mobile group member name color dropped from 30% to 50%
findings.body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). It is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), the same value as .title. That changes the light-theme name color and does not apply the 30% / 70% primary/secondary pair used for the same original lightness elsewhere in this PR, so dark-theme names are also the wrong shade.

findings.title: Category badge notification still scales $primary on dark themes
findings.body: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still sets color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) even though this file otherwise wraps the same call in dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). On a dark theme $primary is already light, so scaling its lightness further washes the badge text out against the dark background — the exact failure this PR is fixing for the other topic-list colors.
